section_summary: The section begins with the end of a lengthy report on Japan’s wartime economy through May 1942, covering finance, prices, wages, industrial controls, shipping, and occupied territories. Later documents relay economic information drawn from Japanese radio broadcasts, including production plans, trade, transport, banking, currency controls, and reconstruction across East and Southeast Asia. A New Delhi despatch submits a memorandum on economic conditions in Japan, while the final London telegram continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese economic conditions, continued
subfiles.about: Survey of Japan’s wartime finance, industry, prices, transport, and occupied-area resources through May 1942.
subfiles.summary: The report continues with a proposed railway route, custody of foreign firms, bond issues, debt, banking, wages, prices, taxation, and the baht-yen exchange accord. It examines materials mobilization, industrial reorganization, corporate profits, investment in Manchuria, and rising stock prices. Its closing discussion covers the May 1942 Diet session, standardized shipbuilding, bond absorption, national savings, and the results of seven major banks.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference file note on Japan’s military and economic condition
subfiles.about: Points to a separate paper summarizing Japan’s military and economic condition.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references an October 7 despatch filed under Pacific War records.

subfiles.title: Summary of Japanese radio broadcasts on economic affairs
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Relays Japanese broadcast claims on postal links, price controls, economic planning, and reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Reports resumed postal links with Hong Kong, Nanking price controls, and a Greater East Asia economic plan centered on Japan. It also summarizes claimed reconstruction and trade in Malaya, the Philippines, and Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Return of despatches to DC/R
subfiles.about: Returns a group of despatches for disposal.
subfiles.summary: Returns requested and long-held despatches to DC/R.

subfiles.title: Assessment of Macrae’s memorandum on economic conditions in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses the sources and usefulness of H. A. Macrae’s enclosed memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Describes Macrae’s memorandum as a well-organized reference drawn largely from The Japan Times and Advertiser. Notes its three chronological sections and discussion of Major General K. Sato’s speech.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Economic Conditions in Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the Personal Representative, New Delhi
subfiles.about: Submits four copies of H. A. Macrae’s secret memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Forwards four copies received from the Government of India.

subfiles.title: Economic material from Japanese radio broadcasts, telegram 50
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese radio reports on budgets, occupation administration, transport, production, prices, and banking.
subfiles.summary: The first section covers Japan’s budget, occupation agencies in Malaya, transport works, a petroleum monopoly, and food and commodity supply. The second covers agricultural controls, enemy property, bank mergers, note issue, regional budgets, and communications. The two sections share telegram number 50.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese radio broadcast economic material
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Forwards the translated broadcast material underlying three earlier telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a translation obtained from Chinese Government monitoring services.

subfiles.title: Enemy and Puppet Economic News Furnished by Waichiaopu
subfiles.doc_type: translated broadcast compilation; enclosure to despatch 792
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Chungking; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Compiles translated Japanese and occupation-regime economic reports from October through December 1942.
subfiles.summary: Numbered reports cover production drives, occupation policies, currency exchange, communications, ports, shipping, banking, food, cotton, and the handling of enemy property. Extensive passages describe a Greater East Asia economic conference and proposed regional roles in agriculture, mining, fuel, manufacturing, and transport. Closing reports present Japanese claims about reconstruction and trade in Malaya, the Philippines, and Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Summary of Japanese economic broadcasts, telegram 105
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese broadcasts from January 4–15 and supplementary November items.
subfiles.summary: Items address silk exchange trading, an Indochina agreement, telegraph links, rubber control, shipping coordination, budgets, power, food shipments, factories, banking, and tax increases. Supplementary reports cover migration, fisheries, Java cotton production, and Mongolian trade.

subfiles.title: Selected DNB Economic Service reports, telegram 898
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Summarizes selected DNB reports on Japanese agriculture, banking, cotton, and synthetic fibers.
subfiles.summary: Reports calls for expanded crop cultivation, a Malaya–Sumatra banking association, cotton arrival from Rangoon, and synthetic-fiber reorganization. The telegram continues after page 132.
